findings.owasp: A03:2021 Injection / A09:2021 Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.reachability: HTTP-reachable at HEAD: one unauthenticated GET to a crafted percent-encoded path, then GET /metrics. No auth on /metrics, no reverse proxy in the verified deployment.
findings.description: The RED counter is keyed on the percent-decoded scope['path'] and /metrics interpolates it into the Prometheus exposition line with an f-string and no escaping of quote, backslash or newline. Live probe forged 'http_requests_total{method="GET",route="/inj"} 999999' and injected whole new series ('injected_metric{a="b"} 42', 'injected2_metric 777') into the unauthenticated /metrics body; a bare %22 escapes the label as route="/quote"test".
findings.evidence: GET /inj%22%7D%20999999%0Ainjected_metric%7Ba%3D%22b%22%7D%2042%20%23 -> /metrics lines 125-126 contained the forged sample and the forged series; GET /newline%0Ainjected2_metric%20777 -> forged standalone line.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated forging and poisoning of the RED counters the project runtime-SLO sensor consumes; arbitrary metric-series injection; malformed exposition body blinds the whole scrape.
findings.fix: Key the counter on the matched route template rather than the raw path, and escape backslash, quote and newline in every rendered label value per the Prometheus text-format spec; bucket unmatched requests under one fixed label.

findings.reachability: HTTP-reachable at HEAD: unauthenticated GET to any unique path, including 404s. No rate limit anywhere.
findings.description: _request_counts is a process-global Counter keyed on (method, raw_path, status) with no eviction, no cap and no route normalisation, so every distinct URL an attacker invents pins memory for the process lifetime and adds a permanent line to the unauthenticated /metrics body.
findings.evidence: Measured on the booted app: baseline RSS 64.2 MB / metrics ~1.1 MB; after 10k unique 200-char paths RSS 70.1 MB, /metrics 3.63 MB (20257 lines); after 20k RSS 72.8 MB, /metrics 6.18 MB (30257 lines); after 30k RSS 78.7 MB, /metrics 8.74 MB (40257 lines). Linear: ~500 B permanent RSS and ~290 B permanent response body per unique path at ~550 req/s. A 10000-char path is accepted and counted; a 100000-char path is rejected by h11 with 400 and correctly leaves /metrics unchanged, so the per-request ceiling is ~10-64 KB pinned forever.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated memory-exhaustion DoS with no recovery short of a process restart, plus a growing unauthenticated /metrics response that itself becomes a bandwidth amplifier (observed 9.1 MB).
findings.fix: Key on the matched route template so cardinality is bounded by the number of registered routes.

findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD - frontend/src holds only money.ts and MoneyText.tsx; there is no index.html, main.tsx or route that renders the component. Reachable as soon as a later story renders MoneyText with a value not produced by the backend Money type; MoneyTextProps.money is typed 'Money | string' so an arbitrary string is accepted by design.
findings.description: The thousands-separator lookahead /\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g is re-evaluated to end-of-string at every position, making Money.format() quadratic in the digit count while the input is only a handful of bytes.
findings.evidence: Measured against the shipped module via vitest: '1234.50' format 0.1 ms; '1e10000' (7 bytes) 36.8 ms; '1e50000' 987.1 ms; '1e100000' (8 bytes) 4152.2 ms; '1e1000000' (9 bytes) did not complete in 100 s (process killed). toWire() stays cheap (0.3 ms at 1e100000), so the entire cost is the regex. 10x digits = 113x time.
findings.impact: Nine bytes of attacker-influenced JSON permanently freeze the browser main thread; no worker, no chunking, no magnitude bound between fromWire and format.
findings.fix: Bound the magnitude in toQuantizedDecimal (reject values outside a sane money range) and replace the lookahead grouping with a linear formatter such as Intl.NumberFormat or explicit 3-char chunking.

findings.description: The inbound X-Request-ID is taken verbatim with no length, charset or format validation, then reflected into the response header and written into every log line for the request.
findings.evidence: Raw-socket probe: a 5,000,000-byte X-Request-ID was accepted (200), echoed in full (5,000,219-byte response) and logged verbatim (request_id length 5,000,000); the log file reached 6.2 MB after 20 requests. 1 MB and 100 KB values likewise accepted. A failing request emits 3 log lines each carrying the whole value.
findings.impact: Log-volume and disk amplification (~3x on the error path) plus full reflection back to the client; the value also bypasses RedactionFilter entirely because JSONLogFormatter writes request_id_var.get() outside the filter.
findings.fix: Validate the inbound id against something like ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ and fall back to a generated uuid4 hex when it does not match.

findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD - no production code calls register_sensitive (only middleware.py opens the scope and errors.py consumes scrub_text). Reachable at the origination story that registers real PAN/Aadhaar.
findings.description: Redaction tolerates only case differences and at most 4 characters from [ \t-] between consecutive characters of the registered value, so any other rendering of the same value reaches the sink in clear. Worse, a registered value that itself contains a separator falls into a literal re.escape-only branch, so no reformatting of it is ever matched.
findings.evidence: With ABCDE1234F registered, leaks confirmed for: 5+ dashes, 5+ spaces, 5+ tabs, newline separator, dot, underscore, slash, NBSP U+00A0, soft hyphen U+00AD, fullwidth digits and letters, Cyrillic homoglyph A, Devanagari digits, percent-encoding, base64. With SALARYDOC-2024-0001 registered, leaks confirmed for 'SALARYDOC 2024 0001', 'SALARYDOC--2024--0001' and 'SALARYDOC20240001'. Correctly redacted: exact, lowercase, spaced-every-char, up to 4 dashes, grouped Aadhaar 1234 1234 1234 and 1234-1234-1234.
findings.impact: The likely production shape (normalise on input, register the normalised value, log the raw submitted one) leaks PAN/Aadhaar to the log sink. There is also no pattern-based backstop, so an unregistered PAN is logged in clear.
findings.fix: Normalise both the registered value and the haystack (NFKC plus strip non-alphanumerics) and match on the normalised form, mapping spans back; or add a pattern-based PAN/Aadhaar backstop on top of the value list.

findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD (no production caller of register_sensitive).
findings.description: _MIN_REDACTABLE_LENGTH = 6 makes register_sensitive a silent no-op for any value under 6 characters - a 4- or 5-digit OTP, PIN or CVV - with no error and no warning to the caller.
findings.evidence: Live: registering '12345' left 'cvv=12345' untouched; registering '123456' redacted it.
findings.impact: A caller believes a short secret is protected when it is not.
findings.fix: Keep the length floor but make it loud: raise or log a warning when a caller registers a value the filter will refuse to match.

findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD (no route raises AppError or a detailed HTTPException); this is the designated egress path for every later story.
findings.description: sanitise_context is a type allow-list, not a content filter. It drops nested structures, values over 200 chars and credential-bearing URIs, and scrubs only values that were explicitly registered as sensitive. Everything else egresses. 'detail' has no length cap and no content filter at all.
findings.evidence: Live 409 envelope returned to the client: pan ABCDE1234F, aadhaar 123412341234, api_key sk-live-AAAABBBBCCCCDDDDEEEE, a JWT, raw SQL 'SELECT * FROM applicants WHERE pan = ...' and an absolute server path. HTTPException(401, detail='bad token ... for pan ABCDE1234F') egressed verbatim. Positive control: the same values, once registered, came back [REDACTED] in both detail and context.
findings.impact: The real guarantee is 'registered values are removed', while the module docstring (lines 13-16) claims context is sanitised - which will mislead the next story author into putting PII in context.
findings.fix: Make context a per-error-type key allow-list, cap detail, and correct the docstring to state the real guarantee.

findings.description: FastAPI is constructed without docs_url/redoc_url/openapi_url gating, so the interactive docs and the full OpenAPI schema are served unauthenticated in every environment.
findings.evidence: Live: /docs 200 (1015 B), /redoc 200 (897 B), /openapi.json 200 (4094 B) disclosing operation ids, schemas and docstrings.
findings.impact: Full API-surface disclosure; low impact today (two platform endpoints), high once the origination and underwriting routers land.
findings.fix: Pass docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None unless a new Settings flag (default off outside development) enables them.

findings.description: No security response headers are set on any response.
findings.evidence: Raw header dump of GET /health: the complete set is date, server, content-length, content-type, x-request-id. Missing Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security and Cache-Control: no-store. /docs serves HTML with CDN scripts under no CSP.
findings.impact: No clickjacking, MIME-sniffing, referrer or transport-downgrade protection for any current or future HTML/JSON surface.
findings.fix: Add a header middleware alongside CorrelationIdMiddleware.

findings.description: No rate limiting and no explicit header/body size limiting on any endpoint.
findings.evidence: Live: 30,000 unauthenticated requests accepted back-to-back at ~550 req/s with no throttling, plus a 5 MB header accepted (SEC3-004).
findings.impact: Precondition that turns SEC3-002 from a slow leak into a practical OOM, and SEC3-004 into a disk-fill.
findings.fix: Throttle per-IP at the app or ingress edge; cap header and body size explicitly.

findings.description: frontend/package-lock.json is not committed. git ls-files lists package.json but not package-lock.json, and .gitignore does not ignore it - it was simply never added. Every dependency uses a caret range.
findings.evidence: git ls-files --error-unmatch frontend/package-lock.json reports the pathspec does not match any file known to git, while the file exists on disk.
findings.impact: CI resolves a different dependency tree from the one audited here, so the npm audit result in SEC3-012 is not reproducible and a malicious in-range release would install silently.
findings.fix: Commit frontend/package-lock.json and use npm ci in CI.

findings.reachability: Developer workstation only; both packages are devDependencies, nothing ships to production.
findings.description: npm audit on the new manifest reports {moderate:3, high:1, critical:1}. Critical: vitest <=4.1.10 GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp (CVSS 9.8, arbitrary file read and execution when the Vitest UI server listens). High: vite <=6.4.2 GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff (CVSS 7.5, server.fs.deny bypass on Windows alternate paths). Moderate: GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9, GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3, GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99, GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9.
findings.evidence: npm audit --json metadata.vulnerabilities = {info:0, low:0, moderate:3, high:1, critical:1, total:5}. Refutation of the critical: @vitest/ui is not installed (ls frontend/node_modules/@vitest/ yields only expect, mocker, pretty-format, runner, snapshot, spy, utils) and the test script is 'vitest run', never --ui, so the UI server can never listen in this tree. Neither vite nor vitest appears in dependencies.
findings.impact: Downgraded from BLOCK on the evidence above. Kept at WARN because npm run dev on Windows is this project's documented workflow and GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff plus GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3 are exploitable there against a developer machine.
findings.fix: Bump vite and vitest (major), or record a dated waiver naming the @vitest/ui absence as the compensating control.

findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD (needs a production caller of register_sensitive).
findings.description: _redaction_pattern is wrapped in a process-global lru_cache(maxsize=256) keyed on the sensitive value itself, so up to 256 PAN/Aadhaar values and compiled patterns embedding their characters survive for the process lifetime - contradicting the module's request-scoped claim.
findings.evidence: After register_sensitive(pan, aadhaar) followed by end_redaction_scope(token), _redaction_pattern.cache_info() reported currsize=2 and a gc.get_objects() scan recovered 2 compiled patterns that de-escape back to the retired PII, while scrub_text had correctly become a no-op.
findings.impact: PII remains recoverable from process memory, core dumps and heap inspection long after its request ended.
findings.fix: Key the cache on a salted hash of the value, or clear/scope it at end_redaction_scope, accepting the recompilation cost.

findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD (no route accepts a MoneyField).
findings.description: The multiplication on line 101 happens outside any try block and decimal.Overflow is not an InvalidOperation, so a raw decimal.Overflow escapes Money.multiply instead of the documented InvalidMoneyAmountError.
findings.evidence: Money('1.00').multiply(Decimal('1' + '0'*10**6)) raised decimal.Overflow in 5.7 ms; every other pathological shape was correctly wrapped.
findings.impact: A caller following the documented contract misses it, producing an unhandled 500 once a money field reaches a route.
findings.fix: Wrap the arithmetic in add/subtract/multiply and re-raise as InvalidMoneyAmountError.
Run with --no-server-header or strip the header in the header middleware.

findings.reachability: Not client-controllable today: the one unbounded client string (request_id) is written by the formatter outside the filter.
findings.description: _scrub is O(registered values x message length), re-scanning the whole message once per registered value.
findings.evidence: Cache warm, 256 registered values: 10 KB message 7.9 ms, 100 KB 79.9 ms, 1 MB 726.6 ms, 5 MB 3611.9 ms. Linear in both factors, not catastrophic.
findings.impact: A per-log-line cost multiplier for a later story that logs large payloads with many registered values.
findings.fix: Combine the registered values into one alternation pattern, or cap the scrubbed message length.

findings.description: redact_values remains exported although its own docstring states that values withdrawn on exit mean an escaping exception is logged unscrubbed - the exact defect SEC-002 was raised for.
findings.evidence: Read of lines 56-71; grep of backend/src shows no production caller.
findings.impact: Leaving a known-unsafe API exported invites the regression to return.
findings.fix: Make it private/test-only, or delete it.

refuted_candidates.candidate: Cross-request PII bleed / request_id bleed via the failure path that deliberately does not unwind request_id_var or the redaction scope (middleware.py:96-102), with _sensitive_values holding a mutable set mutated in place
refuted_candidates.evidence: Two live probes against a booted server with a probe app exposing areg/afail/sreg/sfail (register PII then succeed or raise, async and sync/threadpool) and witness/switness (register nothing, log all 64 candidate PII literals). (1) 1200 requests over 40 concurrent keep-alive connections, mixed kinds: 793x200, 403x500, 2802 log lines. (2) 800 strictly serial fail(PII)->witness pairs on a SINGLE keep-alive connection across all four sync/async permutations. Across both: 0 invalid JSON lines out of 4402, 0 witness lines containing [REDACTED], 0 foreign PII values in any line, 0 own-PII leaks in 808 logged tracebacks, 0 empty request_id on any request-scoped line, 0 mismatches between handler-observed request_id, log-line request_id and the echoed response header.
refuted_candidates.mechanism: uvicorn/protocols/http/h11_impl.py:259 creates each request's task as loop.create_task(cycle.run_asgi(app), context=contextvars.Context()) - a fresh empty context per request - so the intentionally un-reset contextvars die with the task; anyio.to_thread.run_sync runs sync handlers via a copy of that per-request context, which is why in-place mutation of the shared set works while staying confined.
refuted_candidates.caveat: This is a uvicorn implementation detail, not an ASGI guarantee. A server that reused a context across requests on a connection would break the design.

refuted_candidates.candidate: Log injection: a crafted X-Request-ID breaking the JSON log line into more than one object
refuted_candidates.evidence: X-Request-ID values a"b}\c{"evil":1}, a%0d%0aX-Fake: 1 and UTF-8 multibyte were accepted and reflected, and every emitted line stayed exactly one valid JSON object (json.dumps escapes the quote; braces are inert inside a string). 4402 log lines parsed across all probe phases, 0 invalid.

refuted_candidates.candidate: HTTP response splitting / response-header injection via a CRLF in X-Request-ID
refuted_candidates.evidence: Raw-socket bytes: 'X-Request-ID: abc\r\nX-Injected-Header: pwned' is parsed by h11 as a separate REQUEST header, so only 'x-request-id: abc' comes back and no injected response header appears. A bare \n in the value -> 400 Bad Request before the app. \x00 -> 400. obs-fold continuation -> 400. Duplicate X-Request-ID -> first value wins, one header out.

refuted_candidates.candidate: ANSI / terminal escape injection into the log stream via X-Request-ID
refuted_candidates.evidence: X-Request-ID: \x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m\x1b]0;title\x07 -> HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request; h11 rejects the ESC byte in a field value, so it never reaches the logger or the response.

refuted_candidates.candidate: SEC-001 catastrophic backtracking in _redaction_pattern, re-tested with shapes the orchestrator did not use
refuted_candidates.evidence: Four new shapes, cache cleared each time. 'A'*n vs ('A'+'-'*4)*5000: 0.31 ms at n=20 to 2.81 ms at n=320. 'A'*n vs ' \t-'*66666 (200 KB): 0.63-0.64 ms flat. 'A'*n+'Z' (fails at the last char) vs ('A'+'-'*4)*5000: 2.76 ms at n=21 to 37.41 ms at n=321. 'AB'*n+'Z' vs 'AB-'*20000: 7.95 to 28.11 ms. 10-char PAN vs a 5 MB haystack: 40.94 ms. Every curve is linear in value length x haystack length; doubling the value doubles the time. Structural reason: a value containing a separator takes the literal re.escape branch, so the tolerant run and a literal separator are never ambiguous, and the run is bounded at {0,4}.

refuted_candidates.candidate: Backend Money decimal DoS - prior SEC-008's claimed ~10 s CPU from decimal.Overflow or pathological exponents
refuted_candidates.evidence: Each case in its own process with a 30 s hard timeout; nothing timed out. Money('1'+'0'*10**6) rejected in 8.1 ms; Money('1'+'0'*10**7) (10 MB of digits) rejected in 84.8 ms; Money('0.'+'9'*10**7) ok in 55.5 ms; add of two such values ok in 109.2 ms (worst measured); Money('1E999999'), 1E1000000, 1E-999999 and 1E+99...9 all resolved in under 0.1 ms; multiply(Decimal('1E999999')) rejected in 0.0 ms; Money('1'*10**7+'.5') rejected in 82.2 ms. Cost is linear in input bytes (~11 ms per MB of digits) with no amplification - a 10 s burn would need roughly 1 GB of request body. Residual is SEC3-014 (wrong exception type, not a DoS).

refuted_candidates.candidate: 422 handler echoing the rejected input value (a submitted PAN) back to the client
refuted_candidates.evidence: POST with {"pan": "ABCDE1234F", "amount": "not-an-int"} and with a missing field both returned exactly {"error":"ValidationError","detail":"request validation failed","context":{"field":"body.amount"}}; the submitted PAN appeared in neither response.

refuted_candidates.candidate: CORS misconfiguration allowing a hostile origin
refuted_candidates.evidence: No CORS middleware is registered; no Access-Control-Allow-Origin on any response; OPTIONS /health with Origin: https://evil.example returned 405 Method Not Allowed with no CORS headers.

refuted_candidates.candidate: SQL injection, command injection, path traversal, SSRF, insecure deserialisation
refuted_candidates.evidence: Scoped grep of backend/src for subprocess|os.system|popen|pickle|yaml.load|eval(|exec(|open(|requests.|httpx.|urllib|execute( returned only false positives on scrub_text and sanitise_context. Group A has no repository, service, filesystem, outbound-HTTP or deserialisation code.

refuted_candidates.candidate: XSS through MoneyText rendering unescaped HTML
refuted_candidates.evidence: MoneyText.tsx:71 renders {value.format()}, a React text child which is auto-escaped. Scoped grep of frontend/src for dangerouslySetInnerHTML|innerHTML|eval(|new Function returned nothing.

refuted_candidates.candidate: Hardcoded secrets in the changed source
refuted_candidates.evidence: Scoped grep of backend/src and frontend/src for string-literal assignments to password|secret|api_key|apikey|token|private_key returned nothing. Settings sources every field from TRUELEND_* environment variables and holds only service_name, log_level and version.
